static-spa.recommended_path: S3 + CloudFront. Drop the build output (dist/, build/, out/) into a versioned S3 bucket; serve via a CloudFront distribution with OAC (Origin Access Control). Use Amplify Hosting if you want a connected git workflow without writing CloudFormation/CDK.
caveats: Always serve via CloudFront, never directly from S3 — the bucket should not be public.
Use a CloudFront Function for security headers; see templates/cloudfront-functions/security-headers.js.

nextjs.recommended_path: Two solid AWS-native paths: (1) Amplify Hosting with the built-in Next.js SSR/SSG support — easiest. (2) OpenNext + Lambda + CloudFront via SST or pure CDK — more control, more parts. For pure-static export, use S3 + CloudFront.
caveats: Amplify Hosting bills on build minutes + traffic + SSR compute; SST/OpenNext bills Lambda + CloudFront — pick the model that matches your traffic shape.
next/image with loader='default' triggers Lambda image optimization on every variant; cache it aggressively or pre-generate.
ISR / on-demand revalidation works on Amplify and OpenNext but the storage backend differs (Amplify uses internal; OpenNext uses S3 + DynamoDB).

astro.recommended_path: S3 + CloudFront for static; Amplify Hosting or App Runner for SSR. The @astrojs/aws adapter targets Lambda + CloudFront natively.

sveltekit.recommended_path: Static: S3 + CloudFront. SSR: Amplify Hosting or @sveltejs/adapter-aws-sst on Lambda + CloudFront.
caveats: form actions are POST-heavy — make sure WAFv2 rate-limit rules cover them.

remix.recommended_path: Two paths: (1) Lambda + CloudFront with the official Remix Architect/AWS template. (2) Amplify Hosting with the Remix preset. Use App Runner if you want a full Node container with no Lambda cold-start surface.
caveats: Loader/action timeouts are bound by Lambda's 15-minute max; long jobs go to SQS + Lambda or Step Functions.

nuxt.recommended_path: Static: S3 + CloudFront. SSR: Lambda + CloudFront via Nitro's `aws-lambda` preset, or Amplify Hosting.

vite-spa.recommended_path: S3 + CloudFront — drop the dist/ output. Pure static, no SSR needed.

express.recommended_path: Three sane targets: (1) Lambda + API Gateway via @vendia/serverless-express or @codegenie/serverless-express — works for stateless APIs. (2) ECS Fargate behind ALB — for long-lived TCP, native modules, anything Lambda doesn't handle cleanly. (3) App Runner — simplest container path, autoscale built in.
caveats: express middleware that uses Buffer extensively or streams large files needs review for Lambda's 6MB request/response limit.
Sessions in memory require sticky sessions (ALB) or move to ElastiCache / DynamoDB.

fastify.recommended_path: Same shape as Express. Fastify has a serverless adapter (@fastify/aws-lambda) that wraps the app for Lambda; ECS Fargate / App Runner remain the right call for stateful or long-lived workloads.
caveats: fastify-multipart streaming uploads → S3 multipart upload via SDK.

nestjs.recommended_path: NestJS works on Lambda via @vendia/serverless-express but the cold-start penalty is real for large dependency graphs. Honest path for a non-trivial NestJS app: ECS Fargate behind ALB, or App Runner.
caveats: Microservices via TCP/Redis transports → use SQS/SNS or EventBridge instead of those microservice transports on AWS.
TypeORM / Sequelize are fine on Fargate; on Lambda watch the connection pool — every cold start opens a new pool. Use RDS Proxy.

hono.recommended_path: Lambda + API Gateway (or Function URL) via Hono's AWS Lambda adapter. Excellent fit — Hono is built for the edge / serverless world.

lambda-native.recommended_path: Already on Lambda. Skill focuses on hardening (least-privilege execution role, env-var-secret review, Function URL auth-type, VPC config when needed, layers from a trusted source).

static-html.recommended_path: S3 + CloudFront. Drop the directory; done.

hugo.recommended_path: Amplify Hosting (built-in Hugo support) or S3 + CloudFront. Build command: `hugo --minify`. Output: `public/`.

jekyll.recommended_path: Amplify Hosting or S3 + CloudFront. Output: `_site/`.

eleventy.recommended_path: Amplify Hosting or S3 + CloudFront. Output: `_site/` or `dist/` depending on config.

gatsby.recommended_path: Amplify Hosting or S3 + CloudFront. Gatsby Cloud is sunset — this is a real migration off, not a lateral move.
caveats: Gatsby Functions don't have a 1:1 mapping — port to Lambda.

wordpress.recommended_path: Two solid paths: (1) Lightsail with the WordPress blueprint — single VM, simplest. (2) ECS Fargate + EFS + RDS Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 + CloudFront — production-grade. Bitnami AMI on EC2 also works but you own patching.
caveats: wp-admin, xmlrpc.php, wp-cron.php should be IP-allowlisted (WAF) or behind Cognito / ALB authentication.
Use S3 + CloudFront for media uploads via a plugin (WP Offload Media).

laravel.recommended_path: Bref (Laravel on Lambda) is real and works for most apps; the alternative is ECS Fargate or Elastic Beanstalk. RDS for MySQL/Postgres, ElastiCache for sessions/cache, SQS for queues.
caveats: Laravel queue workers go to a separate Lambda worker (Bref) or a Fargate sidecar.
Sessions/cache MUST move to a shared store (ElastiCache, DynamoDB) when running behind a load balancer.

symfony.recommended_path: Same as Laravel: Bref + Lambda for HTTP, Fargate for queue workers, RDS + ElastiCache.

rails.recommended_path: ECS Fargate behind ALB + RDS Aurora Postgres + ElastiCache + S3 for ActiveStorage. Elastic Beanstalk works but is older and harder to customize. Lambda is rarely the right call for Rails.
caveats: ActionCable WebSockets need ALB sticky sessions — or use API Gateway WebSocket APIs.
ActiveJob → SQS-backed worker (good_job + Aurora, or shoryuken + SQS).

django.recommended_path: ECS Fargate behind ALB + RDS Postgres + ElastiCache + S3 for media. Zappa works but Lambda 6 MB response cap and cold starts are real. Use Mangum + Lambda only for small APIs.
caveats: Django Channels (WebSockets) → API Gateway WebSocket APIs or ECS with sticky sessions.

flask.recommended_path: Lambda + API Gateway via Mangum/Zappa for small APIs. ECS Fargate or App Runner for non-trivial apps. RDS + S3 standard.

fastapi.recommended_path: Lambda + API Gateway via Mangum is excellent for FastAPI. App Runner / Fargate for stateful or long-lived workloads.

spring-boot.recommended_path: ECS Fargate behind ALB is the canonical path. Elastic Beanstalk Java / Tomcat is older but works. App Runner is the simplest container path. Lambda + SnapStart works for cold-start-tolerant APIs but rarely for heavy Spring apps.
caveats: JVM cold starts are rough on Lambda; SnapStart helps but it's not magic.

dotnet.recommended_path: ECS Fargate or App Runner with the official .NET SDK image. Elastic Beanstalk .NET works. Lambda + ASP.NET Core via Lambda Annotations is supported and stable.

go-monolith.recommended_path: Lambda (custom or AL2 runtime) is genuinely good for Go: tiny binaries, fast cold starts. App Runner / Fargate also fine.

media-processing-heavy.recommended_path: Orchestrate via Lambda; do the actual compute on ECS Fargate (or EC2 GPU) with FFmpeg / Sharp / Playwright. Use S3 events to trigger Lambdas; Lambdas dispatch to Step Functions or SQS to Fargate workers. MediaConvert is the AWS-native option for video specifically.
caveats: Lambda layers can carry FFmpeg / Sharp but the 250 MB unzipped limit bites fast — use container images for Lambda when the binary is big.

mysql-app.recommended_path: RDS for MySQL or Aurora MySQL Serverless v2. Use RDS Proxy if your app opens many short-lived connections (Lambda especially). Migrate via mysqldump or DMS.
caveats: Aurora Serverless v2 scales by ACU; pin a sensible min/max — 0.5 ACU min keeps things responsive.
Connection string in Secrets Manager + IAM authentication is the modern path.

postgres-app.recommended_path: RDS Postgres or Aurora Postgres Serverless v2. RDS Proxy for Lambda-heavy apps. DMS or pg_dump for migration.
caveats: Read replicas are easy on RDS; Aurora gives auto-failover and storage auto-scaling but costs more.

mongodb-app.recommended_path: DocumentDB is API-compatible with most Mongo workloads up to a version cap (check current support). Otherwise keep MongoDB Atlas in the AWS region next to your VPC and use VPC peering / PrivateLink.
caveats: DocumentDB is NOT MongoDB — version compatibility ends well before current upstream Mongo.
Operators like $graphLookup behave differently or aren't supported.

redis-app.recommended_path: ElastiCache for Redis or MemoryDB for Redis (durable). ElastiCache Serverless removes capacity planning.
caveats: Encryption-in-transit + AUTH token are required-by-default in modern best practice.
MemoryDB has stronger durability (multi-AZ snapshot + replication log) but costs more.

websocket-heavy.recommended_path: API Gateway WebSocket APIs + Lambda is the AWS-native serverless path; AppSync supports subscriptions over WebSockets. For long-lived sticky connections at scale, ECS Fargate behind a Network Load Balancer is the pragmatic choice.
caveats: API Gateway WebSocket has a 2-hour idle timeout; reconnect logic is your job.
ALB does NOT terminate WebSockets the same way HTTP/2 does — verify your client lib's upgrade path.

long-running-compute.recommended_path: ECS Fargate / EC2 / Batch for true long-running jobs. Step Functions orchestrates; Lambda's 15-minute hard limit makes it the wrong tool for multi-minute compute.

s3-storage.recommended_path: Already on S3 if migrating from elsewhere. Use IA / Glacier classes via lifecycle rules for cold data. CloudFront in front for public read paths.
caveats: Public buckets are a footgun: enable Public Access Block at account AND bucket level by default.
Use OAC (Origin Access Control), not OAI, for new CloudFront distributions.

ml-workload.recommended_path: Two paths: (1) Bedrock for foundation-model inference (no infra). (2) SageMaker for custom training and inference endpoints. ECS/Fargate with GPU works for niche cases. Avoid Lambda for inference unless your model is tiny.
caveats: GPU spend gets large fast — use spot for training; provisioned for inference.
Cold-start for SageMaker endpoints is in seconds; size the autoscaling floor accordingly.
